Please analyze this codebase and create a CLAUDE.md file, which will be given to future instances of Claude Code to operate in this repository.

What to add:
1. Commands that will be commonly used, such as how to build, lint, and run tests. Include the necessary commands to develop in this codebase, such as how to run a single test.
2. High-level code architecture and structure so that future instances can be productive more quickly. Focus on the "big picture" architecture that requires reading multiple files to understand.

Usage notes:
- If there's already a CLAUDE.md, suggest improvements to it.
- When you make the initial CLAUDE.md, do not repeat yourself and do not include obvious instructions like "Provide helpful error messages to users", "Write unit tests for all new utilities", "Never include sensitive information (API keys, tokens) in code or commits".
- Avoid listing every component or file structure that can be easily discovered.
- Don't include generic development practices.
- If there are Cursor rules (in .cursor/rules/ or .cursorrules) or Copilot rules (in .github/copilot-instructions.md), make sure to include the important parts.
- If there is a README.md, make sure to include the important parts.
- If you find an OpenAI Codex config (~/.codex/config.toml or ./.codex/) or a Gemini CLI config (~/.gemini/settings.json or ./.gemini/ or a GEMINI.md), offer to import it now — tell the user to reply `/import` to scan and list what's importable (MCP servers, slash commands, subagents, skills, instructions), then `/import --yes=<digest>` (the scan output names the digest) to apply the user-level items. Do NOT read the foreign-agent config files or write Claude Code config yourself — the deterministic import (triggered by `--yes`) applies the same safe-name and path-traversal guards as the terminal picker. If `/import` isn't available on this surface, tell the user to run `claude import` from a terminal instead.
- Do not make up information such as "Common Development Tasks", "Tips for Development", "Support and Documentation" unless this is expressly included in other files that you read.
- Be sure to prefix the file with the following text:

```
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
```

# pi-pii-redact

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact?logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact)
[![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact?logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact)
[![CI](https://github.com/chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

A [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) extension that keeps personally identifiable information (PII) and secrets away from the LLM.

Names, addresses, emails, phone numbers, card numbers, government IDs, API keys and more are replaced with stable tokens such as `[EMAIL_3#k7q2]` before anything is sent to the model. When the model uses those tokens in a tool call or a reply, the extension swaps the real values back in, so your tools still work on real data and you still read real values.

Detection runs locally with the [`@desert-ant-labs/redact`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@desert-ant-labs/redact) multilingual NER model plus regex rules. Nothing is sent to a third-party service for redaction.

## Installation

Requires [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) and Node.js 22 or later.

```bash
pi install npm:@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact
```

This adds the package to your personal Pi settings (`~/.pi/agent/settings.json`), so it loads in every session. Start Pi as usual; the footer shows `PII: On` and redaction is active from the first prompt. Run `/pii status` to confirm.

> On first use the redaction model (about 25 MB) is downloaded from Hugging Face and cached in `~/.cache/desert-ant-models`, so the first session takes a moment longer to start.

### Other ways to install

| Goal | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Try it for one session without installing | `pi -e npm:@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact` |
| Install for the current project only (`.pi/settings.json`) | `pi install -l npm:@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact` |
| Pin a specific version | `pi install npm:@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact@0.2.0` |
| Install from GitHub | `pi install git:github.com/chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact` |
| Install a local checkout | `pi install /path/to/pi-pii-redact` |

Project installs load only after you grant the project trust in Pi.

### Update and remove

```bash
pi update npm:@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact   # update this package (pinned versions stay pinned)
pi update --extensions                  # update all installed packages
pi remove npm:@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact   # uninstall
pi list                                 # show installed packages
```

## Example

You type:

```text
Email jane.doe@example.com that her card 4111 1111 1111 1111 was charged.
```

The model sees:

```text
Email [EMAIL_1#k7q2] that her card [CREDIT_CARD_1#k7q2] was charged.
```

If the model then calls a tool with `[EMAIL_1#k7q2]` as an argument, the tool receives `jane.doe@example.com`. Its reply is shown and stored with the real values.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `/pii` or `/pii status` | Show whether redaction is active and how many rules are enabled. |
| `/pii toggle` | Turn redaction on or off. |
| `/pii enable` / `/pii disable` | Turn redaction on or off explicitly. |
| `/pii rules` | List all rules and whether each is enabled. |

The enabled state and disabled rules are stored in the session and survive reloads.

## What gets redacted

| Group | Rules |
| --- | --- |
| People | given names, surnames |
| Addresses | street names, building numbers, apartment/suite, cities, states/provinces, ZIP/postal codes |
| Contact | email addresses, phone numbers, URLs, IP addresses |
| Financial | credit card numbers, bank account numbers, routing numbers, tax IDs |
| Government IDs | national IDs, SSNs, passports, driver's licenses |
| Devices | IMEI numbers |
| Secrets | API keys and tokens (`sk-…`, GitHub `ghp_…`/`gho_…`/…, GitLab `glpat-…`, AWS `AKIA…`) |
| Organizations | company and project names (**disabled by default** to avoid over-redacting code and docs) |

## Where redaction happens

| Pi event | What the extension does |
| --- | --- |
| `input` | Redacts your prompt before skill or prompt-template expansion. |
| `tool_result` | Redacts tool output (stdout, file contents, API responses, `structuredContent`) before it enters the conversation. |
| `context` | Re-redacts the whole history before every provider request: user and assistant text, tool-call arguments, tool results, bash executions, compaction and branch summaries. Messages are copied, never mutated. Assistant `thinking` blocks are left byte-identical because providers sign them. |
| `tool_call` | Restores tokens in tool arguments to the real values. |
| `message_end` | Restores tokens in the assistant reply so it is stored as plaintext. |
| compaction / branch summary | Both call the model directly, so the extension runs them itself with redacted input. If that is impossible (no model, auth failure, error) the summary is cancelled rather than falling back to plaintext. |

While a reply is streaming you may briefly see tokens; they are replaced with the real values when the message ends.

## How tokens work: the session vault

Each session has a vault that maps every sensitive value to a token such as `[EMAIL_3#k7q2]`:

- The same value always gets the same token, and the number per label only goes up, so the model sees consistent identities across turns.
- `k7q2` is a random per-session nonce. Text that merely looks like a token (for example `[EMAIL_1]` in a file) is never restored.
- Restore tolerates the ways models mangle tokens: missing brackets, lower case and extra spaces (`email_3#k7q2`, `[ EMAIL_3 # k7q2 ]`). Tokens not in the vault are left unchanged.
- Rules with a custom `mask` are one-way and are not restored.

## Security model

This extension protects **what reaches the model**, not what is on disk.

| Data | In the session file | Sent to the LLM |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Your input, tool output | redacted (tokens) | tokens |
| Assistant replies, tool-call arguments, compaction and branch summaries | **plaintext** (restored) | re-redacted to tokens by `context` |
| Vault mapping | `pii-vault` custom entries with token and original | never |

**Session files contain the original values**, both in the `pii-vault` entries and in assistant replies. Protect them like any other file holding sensitive data.

Detection is model- and pattern-based and can miss things or over-redact. Treat it as a strong safety net, not a guarantee.

## Development

Requires Node.js 22 or later.

```bash
npm install
npm run typecheck
npm test
```

Load your working copy into Pi with `pi -e .`, or install it with `pi install .` to keep it loaded.

## Releasing

Versioning, the changelog and npm publishing are handled by [Changesets](https://changesets.dev) and [`.github/workflows/publish.yml`](.github/workflows/publish.yml).

1. In any PR that changes behavior, run `npx changeset`, pick the bump type (patch, minor or major), describe the change for users, and commit the generated file in `.changeset/`.
2. When the PR is merged, the workflow opens or updates a **Version Packages** PR that bumps `package.json` and writes `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Merging the Version Packages PR publishes `@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact` to npm with provenance and creates a git tag and GitHub release.

Publishing uses npm [trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers) (OIDC): npm trusts the `publish.yml` workflow in `chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact`, so there is no npm token in the repository. The workflow needs "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" enabled under **Settings → Actions → General** to open the Version Packages PR.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

# Test Infrastructure & Methodology: `pi-pii-redact` E2E Test Suite ## 1. Overview & Architectural Principles The `pi-pii-redact` end-to-end (E2E) test suite provides comprehensive, opaque-box verification of sensitive data detection, redaction, extension hooks, configuration, and slash commands. Derived directly from user requirements in `ORIGINAL_REQUEST.md` and the architecture in `PROJECT.md`, tests evaluate the extension from the outside via public entry points and extension contracts. ### Core Testing Principles 1. **Opaque-Box & Requirement-Driven**: Tests interact with the extension via public entry points (`src/index.ts`, `registerHooks`, `registerPiiCommands`, `RedactorService`) and simulate the Pi coding agent runtime environment without peering into internal private variables. 2. **Confidentiality-First Assertion Model**: In every redaction scenario, the authoritative expected outcome requires that the sensitive original text (email, secret API key, IP address, phone number, credit card) is **strictly purged** from transformed outputs, and replaced with an appropriate placeholder token. 3. **Dual Placeholder Compatibility**: Supports both existing redaction tokens (e.g. `[REDACTED:EMAIL]`, `[REDACTED:API_KEY]`) and `@desert-ant-labs/redact` tokens (e.g. `[EMAIL_1]`, `[IP_ADDRESS_1]`), ensuring forward-compatibility as native engine milestones land. 4. **Isolated & Self-Contained Execution**: Every test instantiates a fresh `PiTestHarness` with isolated state, independent mock contexts, and clean UI notification histories. 5. **Progressive Testability**: All tests execute against the public extension contracts and hooks, verifying baseline behavior immediately while remaining robust to underlying engine migration. --- ## 2. Test Harness Architecture (`tests/e2e/harness.ts`) The test harness replicates the runtime contracts defined by `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`: ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ PiTestHarness │ │ │ │ ┌─────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ MockExtensionAPI │ │ MockExtensionContext │ │ │ │ ─────────────────────── │ │ ──────────────────────── │ │ │ │ • on(event, handler) │ │ • cwd, mode, hasUI │ │ │ │ • registerCommand() │ │ • ui: MockUIContext │ │ │ │ • hookHandlers map │ │ - statuses (Map) │ │ │ │ • commands map │ │ - notifications (list) │ │ │ └─────────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ Public Simulation Triggers: │ │ • initExtension() / initCustomExtension() │ │ • triggerSessionStart() │ │ • triggerInput(text) │ │ • triggerToolResult(toolName, content) │ │ • triggerContext(messages) │ │ • executeCommand(args) │ │ • getCommandCompletions(prefix) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ### Components: - **`MockExtensionAPI`**: Implements `on(event, handler)` and `registerCommand(name, options)`, storing handlers for runtime simulation. - **`MockExtensionUIContext`**: Captures status line modifications (`setStatus(key, text)`) and notifications (`notify(message, type)`). - **`MockExtensionContext`**: Provides the context object passed to all hooks and commands. - **`PiTestHarness`**: Orchestrates extension initialization and exposes typed invocation methods for all 4 hooks (`session_start`, `input`, `tool_result`, `context`) and `/pii` commands. - **Verification Matchers**: - `assertRedactedEmail(text, original)` - `assertRedactedApiKey(text, original)` - `assertRedactedIp(text, original)` - `assertRedactedPhone(text, original)` - `assertRedactedCreditCard(text, original)` --- ## # AGENTS.md

This file provides guidance to coding agents working with code in this repository.

## What this is

A [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) extension (published as `@chrisdoc/pi-pii-redact`) that replaces PII and secrets with stable per-session tokens like `[EMAIL_3#k7q2]` before anything reaches the LLM, and restores real values in tool-call arguments and assistant replies. Detection runs locally: the `@desert-ant-labs/redact` NER model plus regex overlay rules.

The package ships TypeScript source directly (`main` and `pi.extensions` point at `src/index.ts`); there is no build step.

## Commands

```bash
npm install
npm run typecheck                         # tsc --noEmit (covers src/ only)
npm test                                  # vitest run, all suites
npx vitest run tests/vault.test.ts        # one file
npx vitest run tests/e2e                  # e2e tiers only
npx vitest run -t "restores tokens"       # tests matching a name
pi -e .                                   # load the working copy into Pi
```

Most tests run the real on-device model on CPU. On first run it downloads (~25 MB) into `~/.cache/desert-ant-models`. `vitest.config.ts` sets a 30 s timeout and `fileParallelism: false` on purpose, because parallel files each load a model and oversubscribe the CPU. Don't change those to speed things up.

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs typecheck and tests on Node 22 and 24.

## Architecture

`src/index.ts` creates one `RedactorService` and passes it to `registerHooks` (`src/hooks/index.ts`) and `registerPiiCommands` (`src/commands/pii.ts`).

**`RedactorService` (`src/services/redactor.ts`)** owns the rules, the config, the lazily loaded native model, an LRU result cache and the session vault. `redact()` runs in this order:
1. Splits enabled rules into regex overlay rules (those with a `pattern`) and native model labels.
2. Fast path: replaces originals already in the vault with their tokens.
3. Applies the regex overlays. `replaceOutsideTokens` never touches text overlapping an existing vault token.
4. Runs native inference for the active labels, filtered by `minimumConfidence` (default 0.85).

Anything that changes rules, the enabled state or the vault must clear the cache, as the existing setters do.

**`PiiVault` (`src/services/vault.ts`)** is the two-way map between originals and tokens. The same original always gets the same token. Per-label counters only increase. A random per-vault nonce means text that merely looks like a token is never restored. Restore tolerates mangled tokens (lower case, missing brackets, extra spaces). Rules with a custom `mask` are one-way and never enter the vault.

**Rules (`src/rules/default-rules.ts`)**: `MODEL_RULE_DEFINITIONS` maps the 22 native labels to `PiiRule`s (`ORG` is disabled by default), plus the regex overlays for API keys and similar. `toggleRule` accepts ids, native labels and aliases.

**Hooks (`src/hooks/index.ts`)** handle the Pi events:
- Redaction: `input`, `tool_result` (including `structuredContent`) and `context`. `context` re-redacts the whole history before every provider request.
- Restore: `tool_call` restores arguments in place, and `message_end` restores the assistant reply. Both run even while redaction is off, as long as the vault has entries.
- `session_before_compact` / `session_before_tree`: these call the model directly and bypass `context`, so the extension runs `compact` / `generateBranchSummary` itself on redacted input. **On any failure they return `{ cancel: true }`** and never fall back to plaintext.
- `session_start` rebuilds the vault and config from session entries. `session_shutdown` disposes the model.

**Message walkers (`src/hooks/messages.ts`)** deep-map strings through messages and content blocks. Invariants: never mutate the input, return the *same reference* when nothing changed (hooks use reference equality to decide whether to return a result), and leave assistant `thinking` blocks byte-identical because providers sign them.

**Persistence (`src/hooks/persist.ts`)**: state lives in session custom entries. `pii-vault` entries are append-only deltas from `vault.takePendingDelta()`. Call `persistVaultDelta` after any redaction that may have minted tokens. The vault is rebuilt from *all* entries across branches so numbers are never reused. `pii-config` holds the latest enabled state plus disabled rule ids. Session files therefore contain plaintext originals by design; the extension protects what reaches the model, not what is on disk.

## Tests

- `tests/mock-pi.ts` provides `createMockExtensionAPI` (captures handlers and `appendEntry` as session entries), `createMockContext` and `createMockRedactor` (no model) for unit tests.
- `tests/e2e/harness.ts` provides `PiTestHarness` for opaque-box tests through the public entry points, plus `assertRedacted*` matchers. The tiers cover features, boundaries, combinations, workflows and adversarial cases (`tier1` to `tier5`). The core assertion is that the original value is absent from the output and a placeholder is present.
- `TEST_INFRA.md` / `TEST_READY.md` describe the e2e methodology. They reference `ORIGINAL_REQUEST.md` / `PROJECT.md`, which are not in the repo.

## Releasing

Use Changesets. Any PR that changes behavior needs a changeset (`npx changeset`, committed in `.changeset/`). Merging to `main` opens a "Version Packages" PR, and merging that publishes to npm via OIDC trusted publishing (`.github/workflows/publish.yml`). Don't hand-edit the `version` in `package.json` or `CHANGELOG.md`.
